title: Typewriter and Lantern
premise: In the winter of 1893, Gideon Okafor, a widowed lighthouse keeper on a storm-battered Scottish coast, receives a stranger clutching pages written in the unmistakable hand of a man officially dead — a witness to a massacre that a shipping magnate's lawyers are erasing from every record. As the great storms sever the island from the mainland, Gideon must shelter the stranger, decode the testimony, and decide whether a man who has spent years hiding from justice can risk everything to put truth on paper before the victors' historians arrive with the thaw. The book ends with Gideon broadcasting the testimony in Morse from his lighthouse through the final storm, forcing an inquiry, and choosing at last to sign his own name beneath it.
about_author: Isandro Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs along the North Atlantic coast. They write historical fiction about ordinary keepers of records and the truths that outlast them.

chapters.title: The Light That Answers
chapters.summary: Gideon Okafor, POV. A routine winter of trimming wicks and logging weather is broken when a half-drowned stranger washes ashore clutching an oilskin packet. The handwriting inside belongs to Elias Marsh, a man Gideon watched buried two years ago. Emotional beat: wary curiosity stirring a long-dormant sense of duty.

chapters.title: A Hand Beyond the Grave
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. He questions the stranger, Ruth Calloway, Marsh's former clerk, who reveals the pages are new letters from a living Marsh hiding in exile after witnessing the Ferndale wreck cover-up. Gideon burns nothing but trusts no one yet. Emotional beat: grief for his late wife Miriam resurfacing as he weighs what loyalty costs.

chapters.title: What the Storms Bury
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. She recounts the Ferndale: thirty-one lives lost when the owner's agent ordered the ship overloaded, and how Marsh was declared drowned to silence him. The first great storm hits, cutting telegraph lines. Emotional beat: Ruth's guilt at having helped falsify the death record.

chapters.title: The Historians' Advance Party
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. A well-dressed 'inquiry assistant,' Mr. Vane, arrives by supply boat asking polite questions about wreckage and witnesses. Gideon lies smoothly for the first time in years and realizes he has already chosen a side. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lantern Oil
chapters.summary: Alternating Gideon and Ruth, POV. Working by lamplight between shifts, they cross-reference Marsh's letters with Gideon's own lighthouse logs — which independently record the night the Ferndale signaled distress and no rescue came. Emotional beat: quiet awe that his mundane record-keeping was testimony all along.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Vane confronts Gideon privately: money, a mainland posting, and protection in exchange for the logs. Gideon refuses but lets him leave believing the packet is still hidden aboard. Emotional beat: the intoxicating and terrifying feeling of being a man with something worth taking.

chapters.title: Fire on the Gallery
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. An 'accidental' fire damages the lamp room and nearly destroys the log room; Ruth saves the original logbook at the cost of burning her hands. Suspicion falls on a local boatman in Vane's pay. Emotional beat: sacrifice transforming Ruth from fugitive's courier to co-author of the truth.

chapters.title: Marsh's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. A final letter from Marsh arrives via fishing smack: he is dying and asks that the record bear not just facts but names — including his own confession of earlier silence. Gideon drafts the full account on his typewriter. Emotional beat: mercy toward the flawed dead, and toward himself.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. The greatest storm of the year makes landfall; Vane returns with men to seize the tower. Gideon locks the log room and transmits the testimony in Morse toward the mainland station while Ruth holds the door. Emotional beat: climax — terror, endurance, and the light burning steady above chaos.

chapters.title: Signed in Full
chapters.summary: Gideon and Ruth, alternating. The transmission reaches a naval station; an official inquiry convenes before the victors' histories can set. Marsh dies peacefully, named and heard. Gideon appends his signature and Miriam's memory to the record, then relights the lamp. Emotional beat: belonging found not in hiding but in bearing witness.
